page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.4xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, supplying 16 dedicated vCPUs. Compute resources are balanced with 64.0 GB of memory, delivering a standard ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on external network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is configured with a 12 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual private cloud routing for external communication.

The balanced allocation of CPU and memory makes the ecs.g9a.4xlarge cost-efficient for mainstream computing tasks that do not demand hardware accelerators or low-latency local NVMe drives. Recommended workloads include microservices, enterprise web applications, middleware backends, continuous integration pipelines, and production databases with remote block storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.4xlarge is a general purpose virtual machine hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor running at 2.7 GHz. It contains 64.0 GB of memory, reflecting a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration provides no local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying on remote network storage volumes for file systems and data persistence. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned. With dedicated compute allocations preventing virtualization contention, the instance provides predictable execution for distributed applications. Workload fit includes web application servers, containerized application clusters, intermediate caching tiers, and standard relational database services.
